newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rice import quota should be reviewed-attache.
newsitem.headline: Japan rice import quota should be reviewed-attache.

text.p: The U.S. agricultural attache in Japan said on Tuesday that Japan's quota system for rice imports introduced under the 1993 GATT Uruguay Round accords should be reviewed.

Under the GATT agreements, Japan agreed to open its long-closed rice market and to gradually increase an annual import quota. It bought 511,000 tonnes, including brown and milled rice, in the current fiscal year to the end of March.
"I understand the idea (of a rice import quota) was a special exception," John Child, the U.S. embassy's minister-counselor for agricultural affairs, told reporters.
"My personal view is that it would be highly unusual for Japan to continue this exception," he said.
"Tariffication is seen as inevitable," he told Reuters later.
Japan is supposed to discuss whether the quota system should be replaced by tariffs by the year 2000 but the Agriculture Ministry fears a massive influx of foreign rice once the quota is lifted.
